newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -French debt vols skid, Pibor trade wanes.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -French debt vols skid, Pibor trade wanes.

text.p: Interest in French debt options continued to dwindle on Thursday and with a long weekend coming up in Europe premiums were set to keep sliding, traders said.

Notionnel volatility fell significantly on Wednesday and traders said the levels would come off further ahead of the weekend. For Pibor options, volatility has halved since December, and there too more weakness is expected.

"There are two things which have been instrumental in keeping vol low -- the FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee), which is now out of the way, and the long weekend," said a trader at a French brokerage in Paris.
Brokers quoted implied volatility for options on notionnel futures at around 4.50 to 4.60 percent for May compared with 4.90 percent at Wednesday's close.
The trader said May volatility fell around 0.8 percentage point during Wednesday's session.
For both June and September volatility was at 5.05 percent, unchanged from Wednesday.
The underlying June notionnel future was at 128.40 by 1247 GMT, up 20 basis points on the day.
The trader said there was a little activty in notionnel options but in Pibor options virtually nothing was going on.
A broker at a French bank in Paris said implied volatility on Pibor options was at very low levels but was expected to come off further.
"Vol is around record lows. It has come off from 30 percent in December but it will go lower still," he said.
Brokers said implied volatility for options on Pibor was at around 15.0 percent for June, 17.0 percent for September. Both contracts had come off slightly since Wednesday's close, they said.
The underlying June interest rate future was at 96.61, up three basis points on the day.
"The only thing that might push vol a bit higher would be if the start of EMU (European Economic and Monetary Union) were to be delayed," the French bank broker said.
"That could create tensions on Pibor and then vol could go up. But at the moment it is only a rumour and traders are not frightened by it."
For the rest of this session he said the market would be very quiet ahead of the Easter weekend holiday.
Many markets are closed on Friday and Monday.
